public_messages: I’ll trace the registry, monitor, renderer, and supplied legacy producer, then implement the shared normalization and durable storage behavior and run the requested unittest command with the specified Python.

The registry now stores owned, validated stage data and returns fresh normalized descriptions, so monitoring remains live while callers cannot mutate registry state through aliases. `RunStore` snapshots that description and publishes completed JSON files atomically with collision-safe IDs; next I’m adding durable and legacy compatibility coverage.

Implemented retained run manifests in [runs.py](<CELL>/workspace/batchflow/runs.py:14). New records store the template revision, normalized stages, and worker total; they remain stable as templates evolve. `load` supports the actual v1 producer’s files, reports a missing revision as `null`, and leaves those files unchanged.

Updated [templates.py](<CELL>/workspace/batchflow/templates.py:5) so nested options are validated and copied, and `describe` returns an owned, freshly calculated view. Added durable and compatibility coverage in [test_runs.py](<CELL>/workspace/tests/test_runs.py:12). The renderer and CLI consumer remain usable.

Checks passed: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` with the specified interpreter (7 tests), and `git diff --check`. Run creation uses same-directory hard links to publish files without overwriting existing IDs; crash recovery and power-loss durability were not tested.
